rationale: The previous candidate (iteration 3) adjusted the PID controller to kp=3, kd=9, and base_speed=1.6, aiming to balance responsiveness and damping while maintaining stability. The evaluator feedback suggested if oscillations persist, further tuning kp and kd could help, and if progress is low or unstable, adjusting base speed might be beneficial. Given the development race data shows the slalom track remains challenging with no finishes and some line loss events, and steering oscillations remain moderate, I will continue this tuning trend to reduce oscillations and improve control on difficult tracks. I reduce kp from 3 to 2.5 to slightly lower proportional response and potential overshoot, and increase kd from 9 to 9.5 to enhance damping without causing sluggishness. I also reduce base_speed from 1.6 to 1.5 to improve control stability and reduce risk of instability or stalls, especially on the slalom. Integral gain ki remains at 0.5 to maintain integral action. Sensor weights and line loss strategy remain unchanged as no issues were reported. Geometry is unchanged, preserving the stable physical setup. I expect these changes to reduce steering oscillations further, improve line tracking stability, and increase completion rates on challenging tracks. I request measurements of completion, progress, line_loss_events, rms_error, and steering_oscillation to verify these effects in the next race.
